            • Akshay Patil
              1 out of 5 stars
              Skip the Exynos variant — disappointing performance for the price
              Reviewed in India on 14 April 2026
              Colour: Cobalt VioletSize: 12GB + 512GBStyle Name: With exchange bonus or No cost EMI
              Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
              Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

              I’ve been using the Samsung Galaxy S26 Plus (Exynos variant), and honestly, it’s been a frustrating experience given the premium price.

              The biggest issue is the Exynos processor. On paper it looks fine, but in real-world use it struggles with sustained performance. During gaming sessions (especially heavier titles), the phone heats up quickly and performance drops noticeably. Frame rates become inconsistent, and the experience just isn’t what you’d expect from a flagship device.

              Battery life is also impacted. Under moderate to heavy use, the drain feels faster compared to Snapdragon-powered phones in the same segment. The thermal management doesn’t help either — once the phone heats up, efficiency goes down further.

              For everyday tasks like calling, browsing, and social media, it works fine. The display is excellent, the camera is solid, and the build quality is premium as expected from Samsung. But the processor holds it back, and that’s a core part of the experience you can’t ignore.

              What makes it worse is that other regions get the Snapdragon variant, which performs better overall. As a buyer, it doesn’t feel great to pay the same price for a comparatively weaker chipset.

              Verdict:

              If you’re a casual user, you might be okay. But if you care about performance, gaming, or long-term value, I’d strongly recommend going for a Snapdragon-powered alternative instead of this Exynos variant.
